## 1 Dogs Data
### 1.1 Image of dogs

![Image from Country Living Magazine](https://hips.hearstapps.com/clv.h-cdn.co/assets/16/18/gettyimages-586890581.jpg)

### 1.2 Vectors

```{r}
breed <- c("Beagle", "Bulldog", "Collie", "German Shepherd", "Golden Retriever", "Greyhound", "Labrador Retriever", "Pomeranian", "Pug", "Shiba Inu")
avg_life <- c(12L, 9L, 13L, 9L, 11L, 12L, 11L, 14L, 14L, 15L)
energy <- factor(c("high", "medium", "medium", "medium", "very high", "high", "very high", "medium", "medium", "medium"))
trainability <- c(0.6, 0.6, 0.8, 1, 1, NA, 1, 0.6, 0.6, 0.4)
friendly <- c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE)
```

### 1.3 Subscripting (aka Indexing, Slicing)

1. What is the breed with the longest average life expectancy?
```{r}
breed[which.max(avg_life)]
```
2. How many breeds don’t tend to be very friendly?
```{r}
sum(!friendly)
```
3. What is the median trainability value of those breeds that are friendly?.
```{r}
median(trainability[friendly], na.rm=TRUE)
```
4. How many breeds have average life expectancy values smaller than the median average life expectancy?
```{r}
sum(avg_life < median(avg_life))
```
5. How many breeds have medium energy level and tend to be very friendly?
```{r}
sum(energy == "medium" & friendly == TRUE)
```
6. What breeds have medium energy level and tend to be very friendly?
```{r}
breed[energy == "medium" & friendly == TRUE]
```
7. What is the minimum trainability value for those breeds with an average lifetime of 13 years or more?
```{r}
min(trainability[avg_life >= 13], na.rm=TRUE)
```
## 2 Vectorized Functions
1. `length()`
* **Not vectorized.** `length()` does not operate on each internal element individually.
```{r}
vec <- c(10, 20, 30)
length(vec)
```

2. `*`

* **Vectorized.** It applies the multiplication operation to every element.
```{r}
vec <- c(1, 2, 3)
vec * 2
```

3. `log()`

* **Vectorized.** It returns a new vector where the natural log operation has been applied to every individual element.
```{r}
vec <- c(1, 10, 100)
log(vec)
```

4. `max()`

* **Not vectorized.** This is a summary function and only returns a single value
```{r}
vec <- c(5, 12, 8)
max(vec)
```

5. `trunc()`

* **Vectorized.** It performs the round operation on each element.
```{r}
vec <- c(1.9, 2.1, -3.5)
trunc(vec)
```

## 3 Loan Amortization Payment Formula

### 3.1 Computing Payment

For a student loan of $45,000 at an interest rate of 5.25% to be paid off in 20 years:

```{r}
P <- 45000
r <- 0.0525
n <- 20
k <- 12

pmt <- P*((r/k) * (1+r/k)^(n*k)) / ((1 + r/k)^(n*k) - 1)
pmt
```

### 3.2 Computing Years

How many years it takes to reach a monthly payment of $220?

```{r}
n <- 34
P*((r/k) * (1+r/k)^(n*k)) / ((1 + r/k)^(n*k) - 1)

n <- 35
P*((r/k) * (1+r/k)^(n*k)) / ((1 + r/k)^(n*k) - 1)

```

Based on the trial and error, it would take approximately **35 years** for the friend to be debt-free with payments of roughly $220.

## 4 Future Value of Ordinary Annuity


### 4.1 Function `annuity()`

```{r}
#' @title Future Value of Ordinary Annuity
#' @param pmt periodic contribution
#' @param r annual interest rate
#' @param n number of years 
#' @param k compounding periods per year 
annuity <- function(pmt=0, r=0, n=0, k=12) {
  if (r == 0) {
    return(pmt * n * k)
  } else {
    fv <- pmt * (((1 + r/k)^(n*k) - 1) / (r/k))
    return(fv)
  }
}

```

### 4.2 Using `annuity()`

Calculating the accumulated amount for Mrs. Savingswood:

```{r}
savings <- annuity(pmt=100, r=0.10, n=15, k=12)
savings
```
